title: 32.3 An Accurate Secondary-Side Controller with GaN-Based CGS Isolated Driver Achieving Sub-1% Error On-Chip Sensing
problem: LLC resonant converter secondary-side controllers require precise synchronous-rectifier (SR) on/off timing to minimize dead-time losses; conventional GaN SRs lack body diodes and suffer from current-collapse effects, and accurate current sensing at the secondary side is difficult to integrate.
motivation: Efficient power conversion is critical for server and EV charging infrastructure; improving SR efficiency and reducing sensing errors directly lowers system power loss and heat dissipation.
method: A secondary-side controller with GaN-based common-gate-source (CGS) isolated driver enabling accurate on-chip current sensing via a gate-charge (CGS) monitoring technique. The driver provides strong driving capability with zero delay and precise SR timing while maintaining integrated current-sensing accuracy below 1% error.
key_novelty: First demonstration of CGS-based isolated driver for GaN synchronous rectifiers with integrated sub-1% error current sensing, eliminating external sensing components and improving dead-time loss control.
contributions: GaN-based CGS isolated driver with strong driving capability and zero propagation delay
Integrated on-chip current sensing via gate-charge monitoring achieving sub-1% error
Precise SR on/off timing control reducing dead-time losses in GaN-based converters
Monolithic integration eliminating external current sensors for space and cost savings
baselines: conventional BCD power switches (1.8% efficiency gain)
limitations: Overall converter efficiency improvement, power consumption of controller, and dead-time loss reduction quantified not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Integrated GaN gate driver with sub-1% on-chip current sensing for efficient power conversion
